title: Protocol for cryo-focused ion beam lift-out technique
protocol: Check that the vacuum in the FIB chamber is less than 3 x 10^-6 mbar before starting the cooling process.
Ensure there is no sample/shuttle in the FIB chamber prior to cooling.
Verify sufficient liquid nitrogen in the cooling system’s Dewar.
Open the nitrogen gas flow for both cryo-FIB stage and anti-contaminator.
Wait 10 - 20 minutes before proceeding.
Fill the transfer Dewars with dry liquid nitrogen.
Fill the liquid nitrogen reservoir of the prep-chamber, if included in the system.
Start the temperature logging software, if necessary.
Slowly insert the heat exchanger into the liquid nitrogen in the cooling system’s Dewar.
Ensure that the cryo-FIB shuttle and sample-transfer loading box are clean and dry.
Turn on all pumps needed for the transfer.
Insert the prepared TEM half grid into the cryo-FIB shuttle and tighten it.
Place the cryo-FIB shuttle inside the sample-transfer loading box.
Open the cryo-FIB transfer station nitrogen gas flow, if provided in the system.
Cool down the sample-transfer loading box with dry liquid nitrogen by filling first on the inside, then after some boil off, fill on the outside. Use a funnel and don’t overfill the reservoirs.
Quickly place the pre-cooled sample-storage box from the transfer Dewar into the sample-transfer loading box, then open it.
Pre-cool all handling tools in liquid nitrogen before contacting the sample to avoid melting.
Carefully transfer the HPF carrier into the cryo-FIB shuttle slot with the sample side up using a precooled tweezer.
Fixate the clamp holding the sample in the cryo-FIB shuttle by tightening the screw. Flip the cryo-FIB shuttle up into its transfer position.
Check that cryo-FIB stage and anti-contaminator have reached cryogenic temperatures.
Ensure the FIB chamber vacuum is lower than 1x10^-6 mbar.
Verify that the transfer unit is dry and pumped, with clean O-rings and inner surfaces.
Check the prep-chamber vacuum if included in the FIB transfer system.
Unlock all cryo-FIB stage axes in the FIB software UI.
Bring the cryo-FIB stage to the loading position.
Place the sample-transfer loading box into the cryo-FIB transfer station.
Cover the loading box with a lid, ensuring O-rings and inner surfaces are clean and dry.
Attach the transfer unit to the top lid of the cryo-FIB transfer station.
Align parts until they lock properly for a tight seal.
Turn off the cryo-FIB transfer station nitrogen gas flow.
Transfer the cryo-FIB shuttle into the transfer unit under the vacuum.
Screw the transfer rod into the cryo-FIB shuttle for Quorum cryo-system.
Start the pumping of the prep-station for Quorum cryo-system.
Pull the sample up into the cartridge of the transfer unit after 60 seconds for Quorum cryo-system.
Rotate the black handle to close the transfer unit for Quorum cryo-system.
Turn off the pump and press the “vent” button for Quorum cryo-system.
Remove the transfer unit during venting without using force for Quorum cryo-system.
Confirm that the transfer rod control knob is locked, the transfer unit valve is opened, and the tip control knob is unlocked for FEI cryo-system.
Switch on the airlock pump to pump the lid chamber and the transfer unit for FEI cryo-system.
Stop pumping after about 30 seconds and vent the airlock to open the cryo-FIB transfer station lid slider for FEI cryo-system.
Unlock the transfer unit rod and carefully insert it into the cryo-FIB shuttle for FEI cryo-system.
Lock the tip control knob to grab the cryo-FIB shuttle, then lift out the shuttle into the transfer unit for FEI cryo-system.
Close the transfer unit valve after locking the rod for FEI cryo-system.
Pump for 30 seconds before closing the transfer unit valve for FEI cryo-system.
Turn off the pump and press the “vent” button for FEI cryo-system.
Remove the transfer unit during venting without using force for FEI cryo-system.
Attach the transfer unit on the prep-chamber.
Press the “pump” button on the prep-chamber.
When the vacuum is reached, open the airlock valves gently.
Insert the cryo-FIB shuttle onto the cryo-FIB stage.
Unlock the transfer rod tip to release the cryo-FIB shuttle.
Pull back the transfer rod.
Close the FIB chamber airlock valves.
Press the “vent” button to retrieve the transfer unit.
Clean the working area.
Dry the cryo-FIB transfer station and all tools.
Pump the transfer unit with the cryo-FIB transfer station.
Check that the prep-chamber cryo-stage has reached -180°C.
Ensure the vacuum is in the 10^-7 mbar range.
Place the cryo-FIB shuttle on the cryo-stage.
Close all airlock valves.
Open the “Sputter” dialog of the Quorum software.
Set the coating parameters (10 mA current, 45s).
Press the “start” button.
Insert the cryo-FIB shuttle back onto the cryo-FIB stage.
Check that the Argon pipeline is open.
Open the “Sputter Coating” panel in the FIB UI software.
Bring the system into the low vacuum mode.
Press the “Purge” button three times for at least 0.1 mbar purging cycles.
Press the “preparing for sputtering” button.
Set the coating parameters (1 kV, 10mA, 10Pa, 30s) in the coating dialog.
Press the “Run” button to start sputtering.
Press the “recovery from sputtering” button after sputtering is finished.
Continue work after loading the HPF specimen and sputter coating with a conductive Pt layer.
Check that the FIB chamber vacuum returns to 10^-7 mbar range.
Go to the “Beam Control” panel in the FIB UI software.
Press the “Wake up” button.
Ensure both icons for ion beam and electron beam are green and the “beam on” button is yellow.
Set the electron beam parameters to 5 kV, 25 pA, and a scan resolution of 1024x884 or 1536x1024.
Start the scanning process.
Move the cryo-FIB stage to the high-pressure freezing (HPF) specimen position at low magnification (100x).
Find a surface particle on the sample and adjust focus and astigmatism for the sharpest electron beam image.
Press the “Link Z to FWD” button to safely move the cryo-FIB stage.
Adjust the stage rotation so that the shuttle cleft is vertical in the electron beam image.
Move the cryo-FIB stage to the eucentric height of the microscope.
Set the cryo-FIB stage tilt to 7° to ensure the ion beam is perpendicular to the HPF specimen surface.
Set the ion beam parameters to 30 kV, 1.5 or 10 pA, and a scan resolution of 1024x884 or 1536x1024.
Find the target position in the HPF specimen using correlation procedures.
Acquire both FIB and SEM images for localization of areas of interest.
Save the target cryo-FIB stage position after image acquisition.
Move the cryo-FIB stage back to the previously saved targeted position.
Draw a rectangular milling pattern in the milling control panel of the FIB UI software: 24 x 20 µm at a distance of 13 µm from the area of interest.
Mill away the material around the volume of interest using an ion beam current of 1 nA until trenches are a few micrometers deeper than the intended lamella height.

Reduce the ion beam current to 0.5 nA and mill a second set of rectangular patterns at a distance of 7 µm from the area of interest, sequentially one side at a time with a vertical cut by tilting the stage 1° towards the ion beam.

Further reduce the ion beam current to 0.3 nA and draw smaller rectangular patterns (24 x 3 µm) milled at a distance of 3 µm from the intended lamella, one side after another, with a tilt of only 0.5° towards the ion beam.
Rotate the cryo-FIB stage 180° using compucentric rotation and set the tilt to 30° for under-cutting the lamella.
Cut three rectangular milling patterns forming a U-shape at the bottom and sides of the lamella, leaving only two small connecting bridges (2 x 2 µm).
Mill the material away using a 0.1 nA ion beam current.
Acquire FIB images to ensure the lamella is free from bulk material with exception of thin bridges.
Acquire SEM images to ensure the lamella is free from bulk material with exception of thin bridges.
Sputter-coat the entire sample with a conductive Pt layer as described in section IV.
Move the cryo-FIB stage back to the saved targeted position (7° tilt and 0° rotation).
Set the scanning beam parameter for the ion beam: 30 kV, 1.5 or 10 pA, 512x442 or 768x512 scan resolution, and 1 µs dwell time.
Set the scanning beam parameter for the electron beam: 5 kV, 25 pA, 512x442 or 768x512 scan resolution, and 1 µs dwell time.
Ensure that the cryo-FIB stage is in eucentric position with coincidence point exactly on lamella surface.
Turn on the cryo-micromanipulator controller.
Inserted the cryo-micromanipulator using the joystick controller at highest speed.
Reduced insertion speed when approaching the lamella.
Stopped the gripper tip a few micrometers before the lamella surface.
Opened the gripper tip (∼8 µm) and centered it laterally on the lamella with slow movement speed.
Guided by ion beam live imaging, moved the gripper tip in Z to the lamella-gripping position.
Adjusted the lateral position when necessary.
Closed the gripper tip at the slowest speed until it touched the lamella on both sides.
Increased the ion beam current to 0.1 nA and acquired a single snapshot image.
Drawed two rectangular milling patterns and placed them on the remaining bridges between lamella and bulk.
Milled both patterns simultaneously using live pattern imaging as visual guidance.
Checked whether the lamella has been freed from the bulk material by taking an electron beam snapshot image.
Slowly moved the gripper up in Z to the maximum range of the gripper’s piezo motors.
Lower the cryo-FIB stage by a few millimeters.
Rotate the cryo-FIB stage 180° and set the tilt to 7°.
Move the cryo-FIB stage to the position of the TEM half-grid using XY movement only.
Bring the lamella close to the empty slot on the TEM half-grid by moving the cryo-FIB stage.
Open the gripper tip.
Re-center the lamella with respect to the slot and carefully insert it completely into the pocket.
Perform slight movements in X so that the lamella slides along the slot until adhering to one of the slot walls.
Retract the cryo-micromanipulator back into the parking position.
Securely fixate the lamella in the slot with organometallic Pt using the GIS in the FIB chamber.
Move the cryo-FIB stage so that the lamella coincidence point lies on the Pt coated top surface.
Position this surface perpendicular to the ion beam.
Draw two rectangular milling patterns and place them on either side of the lamella.
Remove excess material from both sides of the lamella using a 0.5 nA ion beam current.
Reduce the ion beam current stepwise (to 0.3 nA, then 0.1 nA, then 50 pA, and finally to 30 pA).
Move the rectangular milling pattern closer to the lamella for each step.
Thin the lamella sequentially on one side at a time.
Tilt the stage 1 to 0.1° towards the ion beam to maintain a vertical cut.
Perform final thinning using a 30 pA ion beam current.
Acquire single snapshot SEM images (2 and 5 kV, 25 pA, 1024x884 or 1536x1024, 1 µs dwell time, single scan).
Do not use continuous scanning to avoid electron beam damage.
Turn both beams off.
Bring the FIB cryo-stage in the loading position if required for the system.
Ensure that the cryo-FIB transfer station and transfer unit are dry and clean.
Place the sample-transfer loading box filled with liquid nitrogen into the cryo-FIB transfer station.
Attach the transfer unit to the loading airlock system on the cryo-FIB transfer station.
Press the "Pump” button.
When vacuum is reached, gently open the airlock valves.
Carefully insert the transfer unit rod all the way into the microscope to grab the cryo-FIB shuttle.
Lock (or screw) the tip into the shuttle and pull the transfer rod with the cryo-FIB shuttle back into the transfer unit.
Gently close the airlocks valves, lock the transfer unit rod and close the transfer unit chamber valve.
Press “vent” on the prep-chamber to remove the transfer unit.
Do not use any force.
Turn off the cryo-FIB transfer station nitrogen gas flow.
Transfer the cryo-FIB shuttle from the transfer unit into the cryo-FIB transfer station.
Attach the transfer unit to the lid of the cryo-FIB transfer station for the Quorum cryo-system.
Pump the cryo-FIB transfer station for 50 seconds for the Quorum cryo-system.
Open the transfer unit valve and insert the cryo-FIB shuttle into sample-transfer loading box filled with liquid nitrogen for the Quorum cryo-system.
Stop the pumping, unscrew the cryo-FIB shuttle from the transfer unit for the Quorum cryo-system.
Vent the cryo-FIB transfer station so that you can remove the transfer unit without any force for the Quorum cryo-system.
Attach the transfer unit to the top lid of the cryo-FIB transfer station for the FEI cryo-system.
Align the parts until they lock properly for a tight seal for the FEI cryo-system.
Switch on the airlock pump to pump the lid chamber for 30 seconds for the FEI cryo-system.
Open the transfer unit valve after pumping is complete for the FEI cryo-system.
Press the “vent” button for the FEI cryo-system.
Open the cryo-FIB transfer station lid slider for the FEI cryo-system.
Unlock the transfer unit rod with the control knob for the FEI cryo-system.
Carefully insert the shuttle into sample-transfer loading box filled with liquid nitrogen for the FEI cryo-system.
Unlock the tip control knob to release the cryo-FIB shuttle for the FEI cryo-system.
Do not use any force during the whole process.
Open the cryo-FIB shuttle clamp.
Transfer the HPF sample into an AutoGrid storage box.
Place a marked AutoGrid into the clipping metal support with the flat side down and the marked side up.
Move the FIB prepared half-grid carefully into the AutoGrid using precooled tweezers.
Rotate the grid according to marks on the AutoGrid.
Clip the grid with the precooled clipping tool.
Transfer the clipped AutoGrid into an AutoGrid storage box using precooled tweezers.
Tighten the box properly.
Move the AutoGrid storage box from the sample-transfer loading box into the transfer Dewar.
Clean the working area after transferring the sample.
Dry the cryo-FIB transfer station and all tools.
Pump the transfer unit with the cryo-FIB transfer station.
Set both beams to sleep state.
Lock all cryo-FIB stage axes.
Bring the FIB UI software back to the default ready state for the next experiment.
Warm up the cryo-FIB stage until its temperature is above 20 °C.
Set the nitrogen gas flow for the cryo-FIB stage to 1 l/min at the flow controller.
Set the nitrogen gas flow for the anti-contaminator to 1 l/min at the flow controller.
Switch off all pumps that are not needed.
Refill the cooling system’s Dewar with liquid nitrogen.
